note: 18 measured regions become 12 rows over 12 numbered exhibits: 10 figures and 2 grids, all of them measured, so this paper has no unmeasured exhibit. The six exclusions are two algorithm listings (p10, p15), the memorandum's page fill on p21 and p22, its letterhead band on p21, and the right panel of Figure 6. The memorandum does carry an unnumbered pipeline schematic at the foot of p21 (input, LM-BP network, recurrent decision model, best strategy) which has no region of its own and is therefore recorded here and in the notes file rather than as a row. Section paths were checked against the printed headings: Figure 1 is 1.3, Figure 2 is 1.4, Table 1 is 3, Figure 3 is 4.1.1, Figures 4-6 are 4.1.3, Figure 7 is 4.2.2, Table 2 is 5, Figures 8-9 are 6 and Figure 10 sits under the unnumbered Appendices heading on p25. Caption side comes from PDF word search, all ten figure captions below and both grid captions above. Figures 8 and 9 are surface meshes, which the captions never say.
rules: Two schematics open the paper and two close it: Figures 1 and 2 promise the model in 1.3 and 1.4, Figures 3, 4 and 7 draw its mechanism inside chapter 4, and nothing schematic appears after 4.2.2 - from 4.1.3 on the paper only plots [place.section_path] [geometry.family].

The result sections get charts, but not many: 4.1.3 holds the fit-accuracy scatter and the prediction overlay, chapter 6 holds the two cost surfaces, and the appendix repeats the fit-accuracy scatter for bitcoin. Ten figures for a five-year trading model is sparse, and five of the ten are diagrams rather than plots [geometry.family].

The paper is three-dimensional exactly twice and never says so in words: Figures 8 and 9 are MATLAB perspective surfaces with a jet gradient over the two commission ratios, and no other exhibit has a perspective frame, a mesh or an isometric projection [geometry.three_d].

No exhibit encodes a value in colour: the two surfaces shade by height, which is the surface itself, and no plate carries a colour bar inside its measured box. Colour elsewhere is identity only - blue actual against red predicted - and in Figure 3 the red YES/NO labels [geometry.colorbar].

Panel structure appears only where one exhibit has to prove reproducibility: both fit-accuracy plates are 2x2 panels (Training, Validation, Test, All) under a single caption, Figure 6 is two asset panels side by side, and Figure 7 is a two-row calendar strip. No panel shares an axis with its neighbour [geometry.panel_count] [geometry.panel_layout] [geometry.shared_axes].

Keys are almost absent: only the fit-accuracy plates (inside every panel) and Figure 6's right panel carry one, and the seven remaining figure rows have none at all - including Figure 6's own left panel, whose two coloured lines are explained only by the panel to its right [geometry.legend].

Printed numbers appear where the drawing is a measurement rather than a picture: the R values in the two fit-accuracy plates, the axis ticks and z scale of the surfaces, and the cursor tooltip of Figure 8, which is the only data label in the paper [geometry.printed_numbers] [geometry.data_labels].

Caption side is uniform in this paper: all ten figure captions print BELOW their artwork and both grid captions print ABOVE their grid, with no above-case figure at all - the opposite of the 2022 papers where a first-figure caption often sits above the plate [caption.position].

Captions are the colon form on all twelve - 'Figure N: <noun phrase>' and 'Table N: <noun phrase>' - running 4 to 12 words, single sentences with no finite verb, no unit, no variable and no conclusion, and two of them name the method instead of the object ('Algorithm flow chart of LM-BP', 'Fit Accuracy Plot for Gold') [caption.numbering] [caption.words] [caption.conditions] [caption.units] [caption.variables] [caption.concludes].

The caption states the case it was drawn under only for the two sensitivity surfaces ('Fixed strategy', 'Strategies vary with transaction costs'), which is the paper's way of telling the reader the two plates differ in their trading rule rather than in their data [caption.conditions].

Pointing is overwhelmingly deictic: eight of the twelve exhibits are introduced by a sentence that names the exhibit and no number ('The figure below shows the topology', 'the line chart as shown below', 'make the following table', 'We have plotted the relationship'), two are cited by number (Figures 1 and 2), and two are never pointed at (Figures 7 and 10) [mention.style] [mention.lead_pattern] [mention.count].

Two exhibits are announced a page early and one of them is announced before it exists: Figure 1's pointer closes 1.3 on p4, Figure 2's closes 1.4 on p5, Figure 3's closes 4.1.1 on p8 and Figures 5 and 6 share a pointer at the foot of p11 - five rows carry `lead_pages` 1 [mention.first_page] [mention.lead_pages].

Reading sentences are added only sometimes and always after the pointer, except once: Figure 10's reading sentence prints ABOVE its caption in the appendix, so the appendix tells the reader the R values before naming the plot [mention.trail_sentence] [mention.read_sentences].

Both grids are two-block booktabs with no rule between body rows, no zebra, no merge, no diagonal header and no note row; units appear once, inside Table 2's 'Asset Value ($)' header cell, and Table 1 has no units at all [table.rule_style] [table.zebra] [table.merged_cells] [table.units_in_header] [table.note_sentence].

Grid shape is set by the number of symbols and the number of competitors, not by any presentation rule: ten symbol rows against ten ranked strategies, two columns against four [table.rows] [table.cols] [table.width].
